note: Lighting order for the hanukkiah and the blessing texts. Blessings are copied from data/corpus/registry.json (ids hanukkah-candle, hanukkah-nissim, shehecheyanu) with the divine Name written as ה׳. They are shown as text only and never voiced in this game.

order.place: Put the candles in from right to left: night 1 uses the right-most holder, and each night adds one holder to its left.
order.light: Light the shamash first. Then light from left to right: the newest candle (the one added tonight) first.
order.shamash: The shamash (שַׁמָּשׁ, helper) is the ninth candle. It lights the others and sits apart, higher or to the side.

blessings.name: Lehadlik Ner
blessings.he: בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה ה׳ אֱלֹהֵינוּ מֶלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם אֲשֶׁר קִדְּשָׁנוּ בְּמִצְוֹתָיו וְצִוָּנוּ לְהַדְלִיק נֵר חֲנֻכָּה׃
blessings.en: Blessed are you, LORD our God, king of the world, who made us holy with his commandments and commanded us to light the Hanukkah light.
blessings.variant: Many Reform prayer books say נֵר שֶׁל חֲנֻכָּה (ner shel Chanukah); the registry text says נֵר חֲנֻכָּה.

blessings.name: She'asah Nissim
blessings.he: בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה ה׳ אֱלֹהֵינוּ מֶלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם שֶׁעָשָׂה נִסִּים לַאֲבוֹתֵינוּ בַּיָּמִים הָהֵם בַּזְּמַן הַזֶּה׃
blessings.en: Blessed are you, LORD our God, king of the world, who performed miracles for our ancestors in those days, at this time.

blessings.name: Shehecheyanu
blessings.he: בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה ה׳ אֱלֹהֵינוּ מֶלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם שֶׁהֶחֱיָינוּ וְקִיְּמָנוּ וְהִגִּיעָנוּ לַזְּמַן הַזֶּה׃
blessings.en: Blessed are you, LORD our God, king of the world, who has kept us alive, sustained us, and brought us to this time.

afterNote: At home the Hanukkah lights are left to burn down on their own, for at least half an hour after nightfall, and are not used for anything else. The blow-out in this game is only for the game candles, to end the round.
review: Blow-out moment: the owner asked for it. The game says plainly that real Hanukkah lights are left to burn down, and the blow-out is for game candles only. Please confirm this framing.
The shamash is drawn in the middle, raised. Many hanukkiot put it at one end instead; both are correct.
